subtopics.title: Surface area of right prisms
subtopics.exposition: A right prism is a geometric solid that has a polygon as its base and vertical faces perpendicular to the base. A triangular prism has a triangle as its base. A rectangular prism has a rectangle as its base. A cube is a rectangular prism with all its sides of equal length. Surface area is the total area of the exposed or outer surfaces of a prism. A solid that is unfolded like a cardboard box is called a net. The base and the top surface of a right prism are the same shape and size. When a triangular prism is unfolded into a net, it has two faces that are triangles and three faces that are rectangles. A rectangular prism unfolded into a net is made up of six rectangles. A cube unfolded into a net is made up of six identical squares. A triangular prism unfolded into a net is made up of two triangles and three rectangles. In the net of a triangular prism, the sum of the lengths of the rectangles is equal to the perimeter of the triangles. To calculate the surface area of a prism, unfold it into a net so each face can be seen, calculate the area of each face, and add all the areas together. To calculate the surface area of a triangular prism, find the area of each triangle and each rectangle in the net and add them together. Worked example method for a rectangular prism: first sketch and label the net of the prism. Next, find the areas of the different shapes in the net. For the rectangular prism, the area of the large rectangle in the net is the perimeter of the small rectangle multiplied by the length, written (2+5+2+5) x 10 = 14 x 10 = 140 cm^2. For the rectangular prism, the surface area is the sum of the areas of the faces: large rectangle + 2 x small rectangle = 140 + 20 = 160. The worked example gives the surface area of the rectangular prism as 160 cm^2, written as a final answer sentence. For a triangular prism, the length of the rectangle in the net is equal to the perimeter of the triangles. To find the perimeter of the triangle, first find the length of its sides using the theorem of Pythagoras. The worked example gives the surface area of the triangular prism as 240 cm^2, written as a final answer sentence. For the triangular prism, surface area = area of large rectangle + (2 x area of triangle) = 216 + 2(12) = 240 cm^2. A right prism is called "right" because the angles between the base and the faces are right angles.

subtopics.title: Surface area of a cylinder
subtopics.exposition: A cylinder has a circle as its base. The top and bottom faces of a cylinder are circles, and its curved surface flattens into a rectangle with a length equal to the circumference of the circular base. A cylinder unfolded into a net is made up of two identical circles and a rectangle with a length equal to the circumference of the circles. The area of a circle is pi r^2; for r = 10 it is pi (10)^2 = 314.1592... cm^2. To calculate the surface area of a cylinder, find the area of the two circles and the rectangle and add them together. Worked example method for a cylinder: first sketch and label the net of the cylinder. For a cylinder, the area of the large rectangle in the net is the circumference of the circle multiplied by the length, written 2 pi r x l. For the cylinder with r = 10 and length 30, the area of the large rectangle is 2 pi (10) x 30 = 1884.9555... cm^2. The worked example gives the surface area of the cylinder as 2513.3 cm^2, written as a final answer sentence. For the cylinder, surface area = area of large rectangle + (2 x area of circle) = 1884.9555... + 2(314.1592...) = 2513.3 cm^2. The cylinder's surface area is asked for correct to 1 decimal place, so the final answer is given as 2513.3 cm^2. The book writes decimal numbers with a decimal comma, for example 2513.3.
